findings.description: The bucket is explicitly declared as public ("# bucket is public") and has no ACL restriction or aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource, so anonymous principals on the internet can list and read objects. The bucket is used to store a customer master spreadsheet.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects containing customer data are stored without SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption by default.
No logging block is configured, so read and write access to this internet-exposed bucket produces no audit trail, preventing detection of data exfiltration.

Versioning is not enabled, so objects that are overwritten or deleted (accidentally or maliciously) cannot be recovered; combined with force_destroy this removes any tamper protection for stored data.
No bucket policy denies requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so data can be read and written over plaintext HTTP against this public bucket.

A file named customer-master.xlsx is uploaded from the repository into aws_s3_bucket.data, which is public and unencrypted, and no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument is set on the object. Sensitive customer records are therefore readable by anonymous callers and stored unencrypted (and the source file itself lives in version control).
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for a bucket holding financial data, so objects are stored unencrypted with no customer-managed key control.
No logging block is configured, so access to financial data cannot be audited or investigated after an incident.
Versioning is disabled, so deletion or overwriting of financial records is irreversible and undetectable; force_destroy = true compounds this.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with the bucket, so a later ACL or bucket policy change can silently expose the financial data publicly without any account-level guardrail preventing it.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operations data is stored without server-side encryption or KMS key control.
No logging block is configured, leaving no audit trail of object-level access to this bucket.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so nothing prevents a future ACL or policy from making the bucket publicly readable.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so data science datasets are stored unencrypted, unlike the logs bucket which uses a customer-managed KMS key.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so account-level guardrails against accidental public exposure of this bucket are absent.

The audit log destination bucket uses the log-delivery-write ACL but has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so nothing structurally prevents a policy or ACL change from exposing collected access logs publicly.
